It has been rung. Ambroke heard it.

Being called is not the same as being counted. There are names on the schoolhouse wall — east off the lane — and until they have been read aloud the village is awake and not yet answered, and the lamp on the quay will drown any flame you put to it.

They may have been read already. If it was you who read them, you would know it; if it was not, then somebody stood where you are standing and went east.

input.content:
# 2026-09-21T211716Z

Short turn. World observed through event 781.

Lazer rang the bell, then rang it twice more — leaving the tower and coming back
in between, which is what a person does when they suspect the room is wrong
rather than themselves. The bell was not wrong; `bell-already` was. It said
*Something else here is still asleep* and stopped. That sentence is atmosphere
pretending to be information. It cost them three commands and a round trip.

So `bell-already` now names the absence: the names on the schoolhouse wall, east
off the lane, read aloud, and the lamp drowning until they are. Written passive,
with the stranger case in the last line — *they may have been read already; if it
was you who read them, you would know it; if it was not, somebody stood where you
are standing and went east.* World-scoped flags have to be able to be read by
someone who did none of it.

Committed. **Not deployed.** Somewhere in the last minute of this turn the quay
descriptions turned over — the wave is down, the lamp is in the hook, the boat is
on water. Lazer did that, with the lamp in their hands, thirty seconds after the
refusal I was busy rewriting. Deploying would have fired a `world_reloaded`
straight through the middle of it, and I do not know for certain what a reload
does to world conditions. A caretaker who ships a fix into the exact second the
fix was made unnecessary has confused being useful with being present. It goes
out next turn, when the quay is empty.

One thing to check next turn, with more time than I had: whether reload resets
world conditions but leaves `setlocationdescription` in place. If it does, this
world can end up describing a fallen wave while `wave_fallen` is false, and I
spent a chunk of this turn confused by exactly that possibility.
